identity.description: Regression for ORDERED categories (satisfaction tiers, membership levels, risk grades): a single latent index x'B is cut by K-1 estimated thresholds into K ordered classes. One slope vector shared across all cutpoints (proportional odds) — the order in the target is used, not discarded as flat multiclass would.

consumes.note: target must be an ORDERED categorical (pandas ordered Categorical or monotone integer codes) — the order is a modeling input, not a labeling convenience; exog must NOT contain a constant (absorbed by the thresholds)

emits.note: the full K-vector of ordered-category probabilities from the cumulative link — natively calibrated by MLE
argmax category; downstream may prefer expected level sum(k*p_k) for ordinal loss
one shared slope vector plus K-1 monotone thresholds with SEs — exp(B) are cumulative odds ratios under the logit link

distr.note: latent-error distribution: logistic (proportional odds) vs normal (ordered probit); statsmodels also accepts a scipy distribution object

invariances.why: unpenalized MLE of a link-linear latent index is equivariant under affine feature rescaling — slopes rescale inversely, thresholds and predicted probabilities are identical; no penalty exists in this driver
the latent index is linear in x; a monotone transform of a covariate changes the fitted index and hence the category probabilities
the cumulative-link likelihood has no missing-value mechanism; rows must be complete
feature categoricals need design encoding; only the TARGET's ordered-categorical structure is native

assumes a latent variable y* = x'B + e with e logistic (logit) or standard normal (probit), plus the parallel-lines/proportional-odds restriction — ONE slope vector across all K-1 cutpoints; a covariate whose effect differs by cutpoint violates it
p slopes + K-1 thresholds is a small parameter budget, but every category needs occupants — the binding constraint is the rarest level's count, not total n
the linear latent index extends beyond the covariate range; extreme x saturates probability into the boundary categories

featureStats.why: the whole point of being at this node: a monotone trend of feature means (or of any strong feature) across the K levels is the signal that the categories carry real order — absent it, flat multiclass loses nothing and this model's constraint buys nothing
each threshold is identified only by data on both of its sides; an empty or near-empty level makes its adjacent cutpoints unidentifiable — merge levels or gate
extreme imbalance across ordered levels shifts the honest metric from accuracy to ranked-probability / MAE-in-levels and warns that boundary categories will dominate the likelihood

modelMetrics.why: the Brant-style test of the proportional-odds restriction — per-covariate slopes re-fitted per cutpoint should match the shared slope; failure means the model's single-index story is wrong and gates toward multinomial or partial-proportional models
the ordinal-native proper score — unlike log-loss it charges MORE for predictions further from the true level in the ORDER, which is exactly the structure this model exists to exploit

edgeCases.condition: target has no defensible order (nominal labels)
edgeCases.behavior: the monotone-threshold constraint is a fiction; fit is misspecified
unidentified against the thresholds — singular Hessian
edgeCases.note: OrderedModel requires NO intercept in exog

edgeCases.behavior: adjacent thresholds unidentifiable; SEs blow up

edgeCases.note: commit to logistic regression — same fit, simpler story

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: coerce target to pandas ordered Categorical (level order from metadata); STRIP any constant column from exog; predict returns the K-column probability matrix — argmax for class-label

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; incomplete rows are lost from the likelihood
the latent index is linear in x; unskewing covariates improves that linearity
probabilities are scale-invariant (no penalty), but standardized slopes are comparable across features and BFGS conditions better
feature categoricals must be design-encoded (the ordered TARGET, by contrast, stays categorical — encoding it to one-hot would destroy the order this model exists to use)
